threads.title: Scioto kits: request to price below OPS-310

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Scioto kits: request to price below OPS-310
exchanges.body: Lisa, Scioto Health asks for $10 a kit on a one-year deal (120 kits a month). OPS-310 gives $12.74: (0.275 h x $33.50 + $1.40 materials) x 1.20. Our cost before margin is about $10.61, so $10 is $0.61 a kit (about 6%) below cost: $1,200 a month against $1,528.80. My recommendation is to hold $12.74 and offer a monthly batch build, which Kim can re-time; if the standard drops, the formula price drops with it. Below-formula pricing is your call; Brett is copied.

exchanges.author: c_lisa
exchanges.subject: Re: Scioto kits: request to price below OPS-310
exchanges.body: Agree: no below-cost pricing. Hold $12.74 and offer the batch build; if Kim's re-time lowers the standard, re-price by the formula. Lisa

exchanges.author: c_brett
exchanges.subject: Re: Scioto kits: request to price below OPS-310
exchanges.body: Understood. I'll offer Dana the batch build and a re-price after the new time study.

Commitment: slotting of his 640 SKUs against our open locations (Omar runs it Friday from Paul's cube data) to Lisa Monday. He holds his team until then.

exchanges.body: Ronan, Mike in Cincinnati. The wrong tees on Monday's truck cost my contractor, Hamilton Mechanical, half a day on a hospital job. He's asking us to cover his crew's time, six hundred eighty dollars. Can you approve that, and tell me it won't happen again?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Mike Okafor (Cincinnati), 11/5: Hamilton Mechanical lost half a day on the Mason hospital job from the 11/2 mis-pick (3/4 tee carton held 1/2 tees, face 14-03-C). Root cause to Megan today.

exchanges.author: c_brett

Under OPS-310 any price under $12.74 needs Lisa, and I wouldn't recommend selling below cost. What could move it: if Scioto lets us build the month's kits in one batch, Kim can re-time it, and a lower standard lowers the price by the formula.
